Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-08-27 | AMZN | Overweight | +1.0% | +0.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, built in stages rather than bought whole at 256.26: take a 20–25% starter of a ~1.0–1.25x standard target now, add ~25–30% only if the 251.08–252 confluence holds on a reversal candle with volume under ~30M, and split the remainder above a close of 260.93 on >40M shares and then above 264.11 (VWMA) toward 267.14. Hard invalidation 246.50, cut to half-size on any daily close below 251.08, and no new capital in the 248.57→235.50 air pocket. Size the starter off a stress gap toward 238.59/235.50, not just the 9.76-point stop, because the 1% risk claim in the plan is arithmetically wrong at a 40% first tranche. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction goes to the aggressive analyst; size, entry and add discipline go to the neutral analyst — the same split the Research Manager reached, and the neutral's arithmetic correction is the one point in the debate nobody rebutted.

What the aggressive proved and the conservative never overturned: revenue growth accelerated 16.6%→19.6% on a ~$200B quarterly base; operating income +43.2% to $27.46B at a 13.7% margin (+230bp) through a 31–42% rise in depreciation; marketing +2.5%, G&A −6.0%, SBC −7.6% against 19.6% revenue growth; core EPS (ex-marks) ~+26%; net debt/EBITDA ~0.37x with $176.1B liquidity and ~21x coverage. Structure: higher lows 199.14→225.55→226.16, higher highs 264.50→278.56→287.20, price 7.4% above a rising 200 SMA (238.59), 50 SMA up 20 straight sessions to 251.08, pullback on ~65% of normal volume. This corrects my own record: four AMZN Underweights (08-14 to 08-20) captured only +1.5%, −0.2%, −1.5% and −2.6% of five-day alpha, and the 08-20 review found over-de-risking an intact primary trend to be the recurring error; the 08-18 Overweight (+0.8% alpha) taught that the failure mode is parking a constructive rating while price sits 5–12% above its 10 EMA. At 256.26 AMZN is below the 10 EMA (260.93) and VWMA (264.11), on the 50% retracement (255.34) of the 226.65→284.02 impulse — the entry geometry I have been waiting for, not the one I was warned about.

The conservative wins on risk composition and I carry it in full. At ~$7.80 annualized core EPS the stock is ~33x with TTM FCF −$11.6B and H1 FCF −$27.0B; capex 27% of revenue (~$54.2B in Q2) against ~$80B annualized D&A, so the depreciation bill is still ahead; debt +93% to $133.0B in six months; interest expense +155% with net interest flipping from +$569M to −$19M; current ratio 1.03x; $650B contractual obligations ($78.1B due inside twelve months) plus $109.8B lease obligations. Earnings quality is the largest unhedged risk: 81% of Q2 net income ($50.5B of $62.6B) is a non-cash markup of non-marketable equity that grew that book from $16.2B to $122.3B — 11.2% of assets, self-marked, no observable price, no disclosed identity or inputs; a markdown arrives as a gap, and the July 31 +12.5% session proves this name gaps double digits. The AWS–NVIDIA headline is a commitment, not revenue (two million GPUs in 2027–28, no dollar value, financing, exclusivity or incrementality), and the 08-27 tape confirmed the timing objection: AMZN closed −1.54% on 35.9M vs 21.5M shares in the bottom third of the range after a midday catalyst.

The conservative overreaches only at the prescription. His case is about price, entry timing and earnings composition, not deterioration of the operating engine, and his own framing is a staging instruction. With RSI 47.23, price below the 10 EMA and the 200 SMA 7.4% below spot, "wait for FCF to turn positive" clears only 8–10% higher in this name — the pattern that cost 12–22% of five-day alpha on my own 07-22 to 07-30 heavy underweights.

The neutral wins the decisive exchange. The 246.50 stop is 9.76 points below 256.26, not the quoted 13.4-point 2-ATR budget, so a 0.5x-standard starter stopped out costs ~1.9% of a standard unit, worse through a gap to 238.59/235.50 — that alone invalidates the 40% starter on its own risk math. The 251.08 cut sits ~0.77 ATR (ATR 6.709, down from 9.998) from entry, so noise can trigger it: an argument for a smaller bite, not for zero. And 261–264 is triple resistance (10 EMA 260.93, 38.2% retrace 262.10, VWMA 264.11), so the confirmation tranche must be split rather than taken whole on the first close above 260.93 with a widening negative MACD histogram (bear cross since 08-17, −1.683 and widening, zero-line cross days away). Hence 20–25% starter, the conditional 251–252 tranche, and a split confirmation add.

Unresolved and flagged, not scored to either side: the claimed ~$45B Anthropic–Nscale commitment routing to Vera Rubin rather than AWS (an equity stake marking up while the top AI customer multi-sources away), and the $109.8B lease / $650B commitment stack against a 2027–28 GPU delivery.

What would change it. Up toward Buy: FCF inflecting positive or the capex-vs-OCF gap closing; D&A/revenue stabilizing near 10.0% with gross margin holding; a volume-confirmed close above 264.11 and 267.14 with the histogram turning positive, then a reclaim of 271.58; or disclosed AWS segment revenue/margin and advertising growth. Down toward Hold/Underweight: revenue decelerating below ~15% while depreciation compounds 30%+, any markdown in the $122.3B book (a size-reduction event, not a dip to buy), interest expense annualizing above ~$6B, or a decisive close below 251.08 that turns the 50 SMA into resistance. Explicit gaps: no AWS segment figures, no advertising growth rate, no forward consensus, no valuation inputs for the $122.3B stake, no organic-vs-acquired split, no contract detail on the Nscale claim or the federal AI cloud line, and no holdings/cash context — so all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation, and AMZN should be counted as one AI-capex-correlated position alongside any NVDA or hyperscaler exposure already held.

**Price Target**: 278.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The +0.8% five-day alpha (+1.0% raw) modestly supports the Overweight directional call, but five days is far too short to judge a 3–6 month thesis re-scored on the Q3 print. It supports the entry-geometry and staging argument—buying below the 10 EMA rather than waiting for FCF to turn—but leaves the core fundamental risks (negative FCF, capex/depreciation, the $122.3B self-marked equity book) untouched. Next time, judge the staged plan against its explicit triggers (251.08 cut, 260.93/264.11 adds) and treat one week’s alpha as noise rather than evidence for changing size.

[2026-08-26 | AMZN | Underweight | -2.0% | -1.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: reduce the position to roughly 45–55% of a standard allocation — trim about 45–50% of whatever the caller currently holds — and execute at least 80% of that reduction at market near the verified $260.28 close, completing it before the NVDA earnings and inflation prints. Cap any opportunistic sell-limit at the VWMA ($265.53) at 10–15% of the intended sale; do not leave the de-risk hostage to a bounce the structure says may not come. Do not short — a tactical short below $257.04 would fight a 50 SMA ($250.88) that has risen eighteen straight sessions and a 200 SMA ($238.53) that has risen every session in the dataset. Treat $266.10 as a rebuild trigger, not a stop: a daily close below $257.04 halves the residual, $250.88 is the hard risk limit, and no weight is restored absent a close above $266.10 on more than 40M shares, in thirds.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not in dispute and the mechanics decide the rating. The Research Manager, the trader and all three risk seats converge on reducing AMZN; the trader's "Sell" label explicitly describes "a partial, staged reduction of long exposure, not a full exit and not a new short," which on this scale is Underweight. That makes this a sizing and execution decision, and on sizing the conservative and neutral seats beat the aggressive.

Why the fundamental file carries the trim, and why the bull lost the arguments that price the multiple. The bull genuinely won the operating-inflection argument and neither colleague refuted it: revenue +19.6% against total cost growth of 16.6%, operating income +43.2% to $27.46B at a 13.7% margin, SBC down 7.6% in dollars, marketing +2.5%, G&A −6.0%. But the bear attached a bill the bull's own numbers make inevitable. TTM capex of $173.0B annualizing above $215B, on a 5–6 year life, implies roughly $29–35B/year of incremental depreciation against a D&A base near $78B — a +37% to +45% increase in a line already ~9.96% of revenue, or ~1.7–2.3 points of margin headwind against a 13.7% operating margin. The decisive point is that the bull's own tripwire ("operating margin below ~12% while capex stays above $50B/quarter") is the mechanically expected output of his own capex thesis — a risk framework that doubles as a coin flip. His rebuttal, that the front edge was already absorbed, is incomplete: he extrapolates operating leverage forward while ignoring the lagged cost of the capex generating it.

Three further items the bull never answered. (1) Balance sheet: $4,118M/quarter of operating lease cost and $96.3B of operating lease liabilities turn headline net cash of +$29.7B into roughly −$66.7B of net debt and fixed-charge coverage from ~21x to ~5x; long-term debt is up 93% in six months, interest expense +155% to $1,314M, net interest has flipped from +$569M to −$19M, the current ratio is 1.03x, and $650B of contractual obligations sits against $215B+ of annual capex. (2) The $39.8B of H1 acquisitions — $1,652M to $39,767M, with $24,359M in Q2 alone — funded while FCF is −$11.6B and debt doubles, with no disclosure of what was bought; that is a capital-allocation governance question, not a sentiment question, and the bull's valuation prices none of it. (3) Earnings and cash quality: TTM deferred tax of $41.4B against $6.6B of cash taxes paid, an effective rate already moving 12.8% → 22.5%, receivables +30.1% versus revenue +19.6%, and allowance coverage slipping 3.42% → 3.08%. On a normalized EPS basis the screen's ~21x is closer to the mid-30s, which removes the "cheapness" leg of the bull case.

Why the tape supports acting now rather than later. Nine consecutive lower highs (287.20 → 282.79 → 280.14 → 278.84 → 273.46 → 269.58 → 266.40 → 263.89 → 262.05) against a flat floor at 257.04 is a descending-triangle structure, not a neutral coil — the conservative is right that "resolves in the direction of pressure" is pattern folklore rather than a base rate, which is an argument against shorting, not against trimming. Price at $260.28 sits below the 10 EMA ($261.97), the VWMA ($265.53) and the 20 SMA ($266.10), so the marginal buyer since the July 31 gap is underwater with overhead supply stacked at 265–266. ATR has compressed to 6.82 (2.62%) from 9.98, Bollinger bandwidth has narrowed ~48% in five sessions and the last five closes span 1.3% — a local volatility minimum into a local event maximum, with NVDA earnings and the inflation print as downside beta for the most capex-heavy, longest-duration name in the AI complex and no AMZN-specific catalyst until late October.

Where each seat wins on execution. I adopt the conservative and neutral seats over the aggressive on four counts. First, the aggressive's residual limit at $265.53 is 5.25 points above spot and never fills in the exact scenario — a coil resolution through $257.04 — that motivated the trim, leaving the caller holding more than intended through the event; the neutral's fix is correct: cap it at 10–15% as opportunistic extra and complete at least 80% at market. Second, the aggressive's 50–60% residual uses a bearish asymmetry argument to defend a bullish position size; the neutral's 50–55% of standard is the defensible calibration, with the conservative's 40–50% as the right answer only if the caller is concentrated or carries other AI-capex beta. Third, the tactical short is the least defensible element in the whole plan — it fights the same rising 50/200 structure the aggressive himself invokes (July 30–August 3: 226.65 → 284.02 in three sessions on 129M and 91M shares is the realized-gap precedent), and the conservative is right that a 5-point nominal risk in a name that gapped 12.5% overnight is a headline number, not a bounded loss. Fourth, $266.10 is a rebuild/invalidation trigger, not a stop-loss: a "stop" above spot with a stricter re-entry bar (close above $266.10 on >40M shares versus the ~31M pullback average) is a whipsaw generator at 0.85x ATR. Conversely, the conservative overreaches in treating the $122.3B non-marketable stake as pure accounting artifact — the mark cuts both ways (warrant fair-value losses of −$1,449M in Q2 and −$1,051M in H1 are already visible) and the marks are not a solvency event; and his demand to exit the entire residual on the first close below $257.04 is too rigid for a floor only 1.2% away inside an event window. The neutral's halve-then-hold-at-$250.88 ladder is the correct calibration.

Why Underweight and not Sell. The long-term structure is genuinely intact — the 50 SMA has risen eighteen consecutive sessions to $250.88, the 200 SMA to $238.53, the 50/200 spread is +5.18% and widening — and the operating engine is accelerating on a 13.7% margin. The record is unambiguous that full exits and heavy underweights on AMZN in this cycle (07-22 through 07-30) cost between 12% and 22% of five-day alpha, and the 08-19 Underweight produced −1.7% alpha without requiring an exit. The franchise is not broken; the price is full and the cost curve is rising. That is a de-risk, and it is why the 08-19 reflection's lesson — judge the fundamental leg only at the scheduled catalyst — governs how this call should be scored.

What would change it. Upgrades require evidence, not narrative: (a) a daily close above $266.10 on >40M shares, rebuilt in thirds; or any two of (b) a Q3 print with operating margin ≥13.7% while D&A grows 30%+; (c) a capex guide-down with revenue guidance intact; (d) explicit disclosure quantifying the $39.8B of H1 acquisitions and the counterparty/valuation basis of the $122.3B stake. Downgrades: a daily close below $257.04 (halve the residual), $250.88 (hard risk limit), then $245.60 (lower Bollinger) and $238.53 (200 SMA, coincident with the full gap fill) — no averaging down anywhere in that ladder. Quarterly monitors: operating margin versus the 12% level the bull named; D&A as a percent of revenue against the $29–35B/year ramp; cash taxes paid versus deferred tax expense; receivables growth versus revenue growth and allowance coverage; lease-adjusted net debt and fixed-charge coverage; and any further mark-to-model write-downs.

Stated gaps I am not underwriting: no options-implied volatility or skew to price the binary event risk; no Q3 revenue, operating income or capex guidance; no disclosure of what the $39.8B of H1 acquisitions bought or the counterparty breakdown of the $122.3B stake; the "AWS 37% growth" figure is an unverified author's assertion carrying zero weight; and no portfolio, holdings, cost basis or cash context, so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation. No external tools or searches were used in reaching this decision.

**Price Target**: 252.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of −1.9% (raw −2.0%) is directionally consistent with the Underweight call, but five sessions against a 3–6 month, late-October-catalyst horizon is far too short to judge the thesis — this is noise around a $260 tape, not confirmation. What the window does support is the execution leg: de-risking at market near $260.28 into the NVDA/inflation event window instead of holding out for the $265.53 limit, since price never gave the bounce the aggressive seat's residual order assumed. The capex-driven depreciation and margin-headwind argument remains entirely untested and will only be scored at the Q3 print, so the lesson is to keep the fundamental leg explicitly unscored in short windows and to keep capping opportunistic limits at 10–15% of the intended sale rather than letting de-risk wait on a bounce.

[2026-08-25 | AMZN | Underweight | -2.4% | -1.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN — reduce, do not exit, and do not add at $261.06. Trim roughly 45% of the current position (the middle of the 40–50% band the debate converged on) via limits at or above $258.00 while the tape allows; do not chase the trim below $257.04, because at that point the break itself becomes the trigger. Carry the residual at ~0.5–0.55x benchmark weight: a daily close below $257.04 cuts it to ~0.35x, a daily close below $248.50 exits it entirely (next magnets $238.44 then the unfilled gap toward $235.50), and there is no averaging down through those levels. No new or added exposure between $257 and $264.42; any tactical sleeve must be sized off the 1.5-ATR invalidation at $271.64 (4.05%), which supports only ~24.7% notional at a 1% account risk budget — not the ~50% a 0.74-ATR stop implies. Horizon 1–3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print; a collar or short-dated put spread against the residual is reasonable for larger books given an empty catalyst calendar until then.
